extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (accelerated examination program)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for obtaining and maintaining special status under the USPTO accelerated examination program, including filing, reply, amendment, eligibility, and timing rules used by applicants and examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election when multiple inventions (telephonic interview)
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is determined that all the claims presented are not directed to a single invention, the telephone restriction practice set forth in MPEP § 812.01 will be followed. Applicant must make an election without traverse during the telephonic interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant refuses to make an election without traverse or the examiner cannot reach the applicant after a reasonable effort, the examiner will treat the first claimed invention (the invention of claim 1) as constructively elected without traverse for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview before issuing non-allowance Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will not issue an Office action (other than a notice of allowance) unless either: (A) an interview was conducted but did not result in the application being placed in condition for allowance; or (B) there is a determination that an interview is unlikely to result in the application being placed in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to the mailing of any Office action rejecting the claims, the USPTO will conduct a conference to review the rejections set forth in the Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory period on Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Office action other than a notice of allowance is mailed, the Office action will set a shortened statutory period of two (2) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of this shortened statutory period under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will be permitted; however, filing a petition for extension of time will result in the application being taken out of the accelerated examination program. Failure to timely file a reply will result in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply scope limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to an Office action must be limited to the rejections, objections, and requirements made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment that attempts to: (A) add claims resulting in >3 independent claims or >20 total claims pending; (B) present claims not encompassed by the preexamination search or an updated accelerated examination support document; or (C) present claims directed to a non-elected invention or an invention other than previously claimed, will be treated as not fully responsive and will not be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated accelerated examination support document required for claim amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: For any amendment to the claims (including any new claim) that is not encompassed by the preexamination search and accelerated examination support document, applicant is required to provide an updated accelerated examination support document that encompasses the amended or new claims at the time of filing the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide such updated document at time of amendment will cause the amendment to be treated as not fully responsive and to not be entered. Any IDS filed with an updated accelerated examination support document must also comply with the requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any reply or other papers must be filed electronically via the USPTO patent electronic filing system so that the papers will be expeditiously processed and considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the papers are not filed electronically via the USPTO patent electronic filing system, or the reply is not fully responsive, the final disposition of the application may occur later than twelve months from the filing of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-allowance fee payment and post-allowance paper restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to a notice of allowance, applicant must pay the issue fee within three months from the date of mailing of the Notice of Allowance and Fee(s) Due (form PTOL-85) to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In order for the application to be expeditiously issued as a patent, the applicant must also: (A) pay the issue fee (and any outstanding fees due) within one month from the mailing date of the form PTOL-85; and (B) not file any post-allowance papers that are not required by the USPTO (e.g., an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 that was not requested).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal and pre-final conference procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The mailing of a final Office action or the filing of a notice of appeal, whichever is earlier, is the final disposition for purposes of the twelve-month goal. Prior to the mailing of a final Office action, the USPTO will conduct a conference to review the rejections set forth in the final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be expeditiously forwarded to the PTAB, applicant must: (A) promptly file the notice of appeal, appeal brief, and appeal fees; and (B) not request a pre-appeal brief conference (which would not be valuable because the examiner will already have conducted such a conference).

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final amendments, affidavits, and RCE requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any after-final amendment, affidavit, or other evidence filed under 37 CFR 1.116 or 41.33 must meet the reply requirements. If applicant files an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 with a submission and fee, the submission must meet the reply requirements under 37 CFR 1.111 and the stated subsection requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing of the RCE is a final disposition for purposes of the twelve-month goal for the accelerated examination program. The application will retain its special status and remain in the accelerated examination program; the examiner will continue to examine in accordance with program procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings outside normal examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application becomes involved in proceedings outside the normal examination process (e.g., a secrecy order, national security review, interference, or petitions under 37 CFR 1.181–1.183), the USPTO will treat the application as special under the program before and after such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During those proceedings the application will not be accelerated and will be treated according to the normal procedures for that proceeding. Once such proceedings are completed, the USPTO will process the application expeditiously under the program, but final disposition may occur later than twelve months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for accelerated examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any non-reissue utility or design application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after August 25, 2006 is eligible for the accelerated examination program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not eligible: (1) plant applications; (2) reissue applications; (3) applications entering national stage after compliance with 35 U.S.C. 371; (4) reexamination proceedings; (5) RCEs under 37 CFR 1.114 (unless previously granted special status under the program); (6) petitions to make special based on health or age; (7) petitions to make special based on participation in the PPH pilot program. Design applicants may use expedited examination under MPEP §1504.30/37 CFR 1.155 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form for petition to make special
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should use form PTO/SB/28 for filing a petition to make special, other than those based on applicant’s health or age or the PPH pilot program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form is available on the USPTO patent electronic filing system and on the USPTO’s website at www.uspto.gov/PatentForms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for examination (items required at filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be in condition for examination at the time of filing. This means the application must include specified items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items include: (1) basic filing, search, and examination fees (37 CFR 1.16); (2) application size fee if >100 sheets (1.16(s)); (3) executed inventor’s oath/declaration (37 CFR 1.63/1.64); (4) specification compliant with 1.52 and description/claims per 1.71/1.75; (5) title and abstract per 1.72; (6) drawings per 1.84; (7) sequence listings/CRFs or XMLs and large tables per applicable CFR and filing-date-dependent rules; (8) foreign priority claim identified in the ADS; (9) domestic benefit claims compliant with 37 CFR 1.78 with specifics depending on filing date; (10) English translation and statement and processing fee if specification in non-English; (11) no preliminary amendments present on filing date; (12) no petition that would delay processing (examples provided). For design applications, comply with 37 CFR 1.151–1.154.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition dismissal for omitted items or formality notices
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition to make special will be dismissed if the application omits an item or includes a paper that causes OPAP to mail a notice during the formality review (e.g., notice of incomplete application, notice to file missing parts, notice to file corrected application papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opportunity to perfect a petition (subsection II) does not apply to applications that are not in condition for examination on filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling replies that are not fully responsive
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply to a non-final Office action is not fully responsive but is a bona fide attempt to advance the application, the examiner may provide two months for applicant to supply the omission or a fully responsive reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are permitted but filing a petition for extension removes the application from the program. Failure to timely file the omission or a fully responsive reply will result in abandonment. If the reply is not bona fide or is to a final Office action, no additional time will be given.

rubrics_metrics.name: No general withdrawal from special status
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no provision for 'withdrawal' from special status under the accelerated examination program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a petition for extension of time will remove the application from the program. An applicant may abandon the special-status application in favor of a continuing application, but the continuing application will not automatically receive special status unless filed with a petition to make special. Filing an RCE does not withdraw special status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twelve-month program goal and qualifying final dispositions
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the accelerated examination program is to complete the examination of an application within twelve months from the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The twelve-month goal is achieved when one of the following final dispositions occurs: (1) mailing of a notice of allowance; (2) mailing of a final Office action; (3) filing of an RCE; or (4) abandonment of the application. The twelve-month time frame is a goal and failures to meet it are neither petitionable nor appealable. Certain events (e.g., IDS citing new prior art after a first Office action) may cause final disposition to occur later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prescribed form paragraphs in Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific form paragraphs (e.g., ¶ 7.126.AE, 7.42.08.AE, 7.51.AE, 7.70.AE, 7.71.AE, 7.84.AE, 7.84.01.AE, 7.95.AE, 8.26.AE, 19.02.AE) are provided for use in accelerated examination applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each form paragraph has specified content and Examiner Notes indicating when and how to use it. Many must be preceded by or include other form paragraphs, are restricted to applications filed on or after August 25, 2006 that have special status, and should not be used for applications granted special status based on health/age or the PPH program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper document and fee codes when filing electronically
rubrics_metrics.description: Any reply to communications filed via the USPTO patent electronic filing system must include a document filed using the document description 'Accelerated Exam - Transmittal amendment/reply.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is reminded to use proper indexing for documents to avoid processing delays. Document indexing is not automated; incorrect document descriptions or improper fee codes may delay processing. A complete listing of supported document codes is on the USPTO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-responsive cancellation of elected claims
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment canceling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims drawn to a non-elected invention is non-responsive (MPEP § 821.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since such an amendment may nonetheless be a bona fide attempt to reply, applicant may be given a shortened two-month period to supply the omission or correction to avoid abandonment; extensions are available under 37 CFR 1.136(a) but filing a petition for extension will remove the application from the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for additional information (form paragraph use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph ¶ 19.02.AE may be used when it is necessary to obtain additional information from applicant to reach full and proper consideration of issues (e.g., in response to a protest under 37 CFR 1.291).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to reply within TWO (2) MONTHS will result in abandonment. This form paragraph is limited to applications filed on or after August 25, 2006 that have special status under the program or other specified grounds.
